clue.text: The demon's boltin' his food, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound rather than a spelling, so the phrase before it is to be said out loud

parts.note: bolting food is eating it greedily, dropped g and all

explanation.surface: A demon wolfing down its dinner with a dropped g, like a greedy schoolboy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in boltin' tells you to keep the clipped form, gobblin', which sounds just like the answer GOBLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin is a mischievous evil sprite of folklore, a small kind of demon.

clue.text: Saucy Siamese birds or bird?

parts.note: surface reading: cheeky pair of birds from Siam
setter's reading: the two birds in 'sauce for the goose is sauce for the gander', joined like Siamese twins into one bird name

explanation.surface: A query whether some cheeky Thai birds are one bird or several.
explanation.walkthrough: Saucy points to the proverb pairing goose and gander; Siamese means joined, so the two names fuse into GOOSANDER, which is itself a single bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The goosander is a large fish-eating sawbill duck, called the common merganser in America.

clue.text: Wild ox by Lake Erie?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large wild bovine

definitions.note: describes the place rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the city in New York State on Lake Erie's eastern shore

explanation.surface: A wild ox spotted by the shore of one of the Great Lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second half is a description of a place: the city at the lake's eastern end.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo names both the wild ox and the industrial city in New York State on Lake Erie.

clue.text: Unlike Prudence's behaviour

parts.note: surface reading: the conduct of a woman named Prudence
setter's reading: prudence as the quality of being careful, so the opposite of careful

explanation.surface: Someone acting out of character for a woman called Prudence.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P dresses the virtue up as a girl's name; strip it and the clue asks for the opposite of prudent.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudence is carefulness, so behaviour unlike it is rash, heedless of danger, lacking caution.

clue.text: Plant poisonous to a male bird

parts.note: a man is a male person
a drake is a male duck

explanation.surface: A warning that some plant is toxic to a cock bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'a male bird' as one phrase, a cock; it must be split after male. The mandrake's forked root was once thought to look like a little man.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a narcotic, toxic herb of the nightshade family with a forked root.

clue.text: He hopes to get some post

definitions.text: He hopes to get some post

parts.note: surface reading: someone waiting for letters in the mail
setter's reading: a post as a job or position

explanation.surface: A man waiting hopefully for the postman to bring letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Post is mail on the surface but a job underneath, so the hopeful one is a job-seeker.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is a person who formally asks for something, typically a job or position.

clue.text: Fruitful engagement

parts.note: surface reading: a productive meeting or commitment
setter's reading: an engagement word that is also the name of a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: Fruitful means productive on the surface; read it as 'that is a fruit' and the word is both an appointment and the palm fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is an arranged social appointment, and also the sweet fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: Can I be friendly?

parts.note: am is the form of be that goes with I
taken as written
to be able is to have the power, so can

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they are capable of being nice.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn the question into its other wording, 'Am I able?', and the three words run together as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means having a pleasant, good-natured manner, warm and agreeable towards others.

clue.text: It's consumed with or without its head and tail

parts.note: surface reading: some food, such as a prawn, served whole

parts.words: with or without its head and tail
parts.note: setter's reading: the word for consumed still means consumed once its first and last letters are lopped off

explanation.surface: A fish or prawn that people eat with or without its head and tail.
explanation.walkthrough: EATEN means consumed; take off its head and tail and ATE remains, which also means consumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Eaten is the past participle of eat, meaning taken in as food and used up.

clue.text: See a bird do it in opera, or a Cheshire cat

parts.words: See a bird do it in opera
parts.note: setter's reading: Wagner's swan-knight opera has, at the end of its title, the very thing the bird does
surface reading: the cat in Alice in Wonderland that fades away until only one feature is left

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch a bird perform on the opera stage, or Lewis Carroll's cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Lohengrin arrives in a boat drawn by a swan, and the opera's name ends in GRIN; the Cheshire cat in Alice in Wonderland is famous for doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a broad smile, and the Cheshire cat leaves its smile behind as it vanishes.

clue.text: One of Evelyn Waugh's gentlemen?

parts.note: surface reading: a gentleman character from some Waugh novel
setter's reading: a Waugh war-novel title pairs gentlemen with another group, and that group is wanted

explanation.surface: Asking which character in an Evelyn Waugh book counts as a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Officers and Gentlemen (1955) is the second book of Waugh's Sword of Honour trilogy; the clue wants the noun paired with gentlemen in that title.
explanation.definitionFit: Waugh's title pairs military officers with gentlemen, so a commissioned soldier is one of the pair.

clue.text: A lover of his country, was Bolingbroke's King

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone devoted to their nation

definitions.note: the adjective in the title phrase Patriot King
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Viscount Bolingbroke wrote The Idea of a ... King (1738)

explanation.surface: A claim that some king of Bolingbroke's was a devoted lover of his land.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolingbroke here is the 18th-century Tory statesman Henry St John, not Shakespeare's Henry IV; his essay described an ideal Patriot King.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is literally one devoted to their fatherland, and Bolingbroke attached the word to his ideal monarch.

clue.text: Handy assistant for a dictator

parts.note: surface reading: a useful henchman serving a tyrant
setter's reading: working by hand (Latin manus), helping someone who dictates letters

explanation.surface: A useful sidekick at the service of a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: A dictator here is just someone dictating text; the answer comes from Latin a manu, by hand, which is what makes the assistant handy.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a secretary or scribe who writes down what another person dictates.

clue.text: No prohibition in Argyll

definitions.note: the answer is a town found in Argyll, not Argyll itself

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing
a ban forbids something

explanation.surface: Someone remarking that Argyll has no prohibition on drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Argyll is a county on the west coast of Scotland; the answer is its port town, home of a well-known whisky distillery, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port and town on the Argyll coast of western Scotland.

clue.text: Bring under suspicion by mutual concession?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to expose someone to suspicion or discredit
second meaning: an agreement in which each side gives ground

explanation.surface: Casting doubt on someone through a deal both sides gave way on.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to endanger a reputation; the noun is a settlement where each party yields something.

clue.text: Humming like a far from busy bee?

definitions.text: Humming like a far from busy bee?

parts.note: surface reading: the buzzing noise any bee makes
setter's reading: the male bee does no work, so the word for an idler's sound doubles as acting like one

explanation.surface: The buzz of a bee that is taking things easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The male honeybee is the one that gathers no honey, so the participle means both making a low hum and behaving like that lazy bee.
explanation.definitionFit: A low continuous monotonous hum is called this, and the lazy male bee shares the word's root.

clue.text: It goes to one's head in the Highlands

definitions.text: It goes to one's head in the Highlands

parts.note: surface reading: something intoxicating, like Highland whisky

parts.words: goes to one's head in the Highlands
parts.note: setter's reading: literally worn on the head by Scots

explanation.surface: Something in the Scottish Highlands, surely the whisky, that makes a person drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to one's head' is the idiom for intoxicating drink; taken literally it is something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a brimless boat-shaped woollen cap, part of traditional Scottish Highland dress.

clue.text: Waders resorting to caves

indicators.note: re-sorting means sorting again, putting the letters into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishermen in waders heading off to some caves.
explanation.walkthrough: Resorting looks like going somewhere for a holiday; read it as re-sorting. Waders here are birds, not boots.
explanation.definitionFit: Avocets are long-legged wading birds with slender upturned bills.

clue.text: Miss Lunn left at the fortress gateway

parts.note: Sally Lunn is the name of a sweet teacake from Bath, after its supposed baker
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A woman leaving someone at the gates of a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Sally Lunn is a large sweet bun associated with Bath, England, so Miss Lunn's first name is wanted; left is a verb on the surface but a direction here.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally port is a small concealed gate in fortifications from which defenders could make a sudden sortie.

clue.text: Transport put out in uncommon situation

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another
a situation is a placing or position, here the spot in which a piece is set

parts.note: uncommon means seldom found

indicators.note: out describes something disordered or out of place, so the letters before it are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then jumbled

explanation.surface: Public transport being disrupted in an unusual set of circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: Transport looks like buses and trains, but it means ecstasy, as in being transported with joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport in the sense of being carried away by delight is a synonym for ecstatic joy.

clue.text: "With prudes for ——s, dowagers for deans." (Tennyson)

definitions.note: the gap stands for the plural; the grid takes the singular

parts.note: surface reading: a line of verse about staffing a strict institution
setter's reading: the line comes from Tennyson's The Princess, about a women's college, and the gap is a university disciplinary officer

explanation.walkthrough: In The Princess the college is staffed by prudish women in the posts men would fill: the gap is a university official, paired with deans.
explanation.definitionFit: A proctor is an officer at Oxford or Cambridge who keeps discipline among the students.

clue.text: New coalpit of current interest

indicators.note: something made new has been reworked, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly opened coal mine making the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical relates to matters in the news at the present time.

clue.text: Hymn for church spoken on one note

parts.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
oral means spoken rather than written
E is one of the musical notes A to G

explanation.surface: A church hymn intoned on a single note rather than sung.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken here is not a sound signal: it gives a synonym, not a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a stately hymn tune of the Lutheran church, sung by the congregation.

clue.text: Vessel made by Cornish company?

indicators.note: the company is made, or set up, by the region surrounding it

parts.note: Cornwall lies in the south-west of England, abbreviated SW
Co is the standard abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A boat built by a firm based in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the stretch: Cornish stands for SW because Cornwall is England's south-western tip, and the company sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scow is a flat-bottomed boat, used as a barge or lighter for carrying cargo.

clue.text: Fight for a remnant of food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: Animals battling over the last leftover morsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is informally a brief fight, and also a small leftover piece of a meal.

clue.text: This the study? Tut!

parts.note: surface reading: someone tutting in disapproval at a messy study room
setter's reading: Tut is the boy pharaoh Tutankhamun, the most famous subject of one field of research

explanation.surface: Someone shown into a messy study and clicking their tongue in disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: Tut! sounds like disapproval, and study sounds like a room; together they point to the academic study of ancient Egypt, whose star is King Tut.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptology is the scholarly study of ancient Egyptian history, language and remains, including Tutankhamun's tomb.

clue.text: Freedom of movement on the stage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slack, as in a rope or loose joint

definitions.note: describes what is put on a stage rather than naming it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a drama performed in a theatre

explanation.surface: An actor or dancer being allowed room to move about the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Play means slack or room to move in a mechanism, and also a dramatic work performed by actors.

clue.text: A slight, but noted connexion with musicians

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an insult or disparaging remark
second meaning: a curved mark in a score joining notes to be played smoothly

explanation.surface: A minor snub, yet a well-known link with the music world.
explanation.walkthrough: Noted looks like 'well known', but it means 'between notes'; connexion is the old British spelling of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A slur is a disparaging remark, and in music a curved line joining notes to be played legato.

clue.text: Snake is an excellent specimen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: informal American name for a rattlesnake
second meaning: dated British slang for something first-rate, as in a rattling good thing

explanation.surface: A zoologist praising a fine example of a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is old British slang: a rattler was a splendid example of its kind, from the phrase 'rattling good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a colloquial name for the rattlesnake and dated slang for a first-class thing.

clue.text: Scorer's instruction: Go at it a new way

indicators.note: doing it a new way means arranging the letters differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket scorer or sports scorer being urged to attack the job differently.
explanation.walkthrough: Scorer suggests sport, but it is the composer who writes the score; the 'a' of 'a new way' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitato is an Italian marking in a musical score telling players to perform in an agitated, restless manner.

clue.text: Describes harbour Illuminations

parts.note: a port is a harbour
rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Someone describing the lights strung around a harbour, like a seaside illuminations display.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict or represent them in words or pictures.

clue.text: Feel contrition, being shut up again

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
pent means confined, as in pent-up

explanation.surface: A prisoner feeling sorry once locked up a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel sorrow and regret for one's wrongdoing.
